correctness.rationale: A complete five-step proof establishes conditional design unbiasedness, Gaussian conditional error, OLS Student mixture via Schur complement plus Cramer--Wold, exact inverse-beta moment spectrum, and a unique continuous pilot risk minimum with verified integer-neighbor rule. Tests in standalone verify.py passed 4675 checks. Pilot a=p or p+1 correctly gives infinite unconditional second moment despite finite almost-sure observations. No finite-test-to-infinite inference.

originality.rationale: Originality is asserted only for the integrated exact Gaussian two-stage gradient-estimation law (Student scale mixture, all moments, finite-population risk and optimized pilot split). The originating 2026 paper states the estimator but not this calculation; classical constituent identities are explicitly attributed, and possible specialized survey precedents remain a residual risk. Sanguiao Sande--Zhang (2020 preprint, 2021 journal) previously proved the exact general unbiased single-split estimator and Riaño (2026) contrasts it with a different general variance framework; neither is credited as a new estimator herein.
residual_risks: The Sitter 1997 two-phase survey regression article was only accessible in abstract; its detailed formulas could have overlapping Gaussian specializations.

Generalized regression estimators, Gaussian inverse-Wishart risk, Student laws and split-sample control variates are classical; the novelty case depends on the combined algorithm-specific exact result, not on these ingredients.
Search coverage cannot prove no other unindexed paper derives the same exact combination.
Only the directly relevant portions of the 23-page 2020 design-unbiased survey paper were materially inspected; unexamined sections remain a small possible specialization overlap risk.

value.rationale: The source gradient method spends part of its actual sampling budget learning a predictor. This theorem shows a sharp moment-collapse boundary for unregularized linear pilots and, at equal gradient-query count, a nontrivial exact pilot allocation and signal-to-noise criterion for improved accuracy. It is a motivated reliability/resource benchmark, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no improvement of the source KRR implementation is claimed.
